patch.value: Published GitHub releases remain mutable, so daily-release immutability is policy-only instead of platform-enforced

The sole v2026.8.15 GitHub release is correctly unique and its npm artifact is published, but GitHub reports isImmutable:false. GitHub now supports repository-level immutable releases for future publications, locking release assets and tags and producing release attestations. The release system must enable that control and make the immutable state an executable publication/verification contract without creating a second automatic release in one UTC day.

Repository or organization policy enables GitHub release immutability for future releases; publication stages every required asset in a draft before publishing; the release gate verifies the published record is immutable and binds the tag, commit SHA, assets, checksums, and release attestation; a negative control proves the workflow refuses to advertise success when immutability is absent or unverifiable; tag movement, tag deletion, asset mutation, and same-name tag reuse protections are covered by executable evidence where the platform permits; one automatic release per UTC day remains enforced while explicitly manual same-day releases retain their separately governed path; npm latest, npx, bunx, and direct package installation resolve the same version and do not trigger additional publication; recovery behavior is documented for failures before publication because assets cannot be appended afterward; local and hosted gates consume the same SDK contract and emit compact machine-readable receipts; release-health monitoring alerts on policy drift without attempting destructive repair; public documentation explains the immutable-release trust boundary without credentials or host-specific operations.
Make every published daily release cryptographically and operationally trustworthy across GitHub, npm, npx, and bunx.
Enable GitHub immutable releases and gate every future publication on verifiable tag, asset, attestation, and consumer identity.
Closes the gap between the project's immutable-release promise and the platform state consumers can independently verify.
Prevents post-publication tag and asset tampering, strengthens provenance, and makes release integrity machine-checkable.
Future daily releases report immutable state, carry verifiable attestations, and pass exact-artifact consumer checks without duplicate publication.
The live daily release succeeded today but exposed isImmutable:false, and GitHub's supported immutable-release control only protects future publications after it is enabled.
GitHub.com Releases, GitHub Actions auto-release and recovery workflows, npm registry, npx and bunx consumers

Run gh release list with the isImmutable field for v2026.8.15; observe isImmutable:false despite a unique successful daily release. Compare with GitHub's repository immutable-release capability, which applies to future releases.
Every future published GitHub release is platform-immutable and its exact tag, commit, assets, attestation, npm artifact, npx result, and bunx result are verified by one shared SDK-backed gate.
v2026.8.15 is unique and published successfully, but GitHub reports isImmutable:false, so tags and assets lack the platform-enforced immutable-release guarantee.

Consumers currently depend on repository permissions and workflow discipline to prevent post-publication tag or asset mutation; the GitHub release record does not supply the strongest available tamper-evident guarantee.
